reachable: Yes, at the scored position specifically. build_cups_layout puts the read at rpos = 2*r, an even (command) index, and the module adds its contribution to pred[:, 0::2, :] — so the transport read lands on exactly the vector the N-way pick is taken from. Verified by execution: (a) the child's prediction at the read differs from the parent r22's by 0.0078 against a parent prediction scale of 0.468 at init, so the channel is live from step 1, not zero-init; the measured init gate is 0.263 (claimed ~0.027 * v_read after the 0.1*I readout — confirmed, tp_out diag = 0.100). (b) Gradient reaches every new parameter on the first backward through the read position: tp_share 1.7e-3, tp_dst 1.7e-3, tp_src 9.8e-5, tp_out 3.3e-2, tp_move 2.4e-5, tp_erase 2.8e-5, tp_write 3.7e-4, tp_gate 3.0e-4, tp_logit_decay 2.0e-6. (c) The training loss is taken on cmd-position predictions (harness._train: cmd_pred[m]), so the channel is under the main loss. (d) The optim routing claims check out by executing the optim's own selection rules on the built net: Muon captures tp_share/tp_src/tp_dst (all (64,176)), the spectral cap captures tp_out (768,768). (e) The r23 head stays live — _attn_surface_ok(net) is True and head.wrap returns _disabled=False, as claimed. (f) Inherited parameters are bit-identical to the r22 parent at the same seed, so the new modules do not disturb the init RNG stream.
solves_outside_model: No. The module's only inputs are tok_emb (raw command/observation embeddings) and h_out from the trunk; it contains no string handling, no file or dataset access, no imports beyond math/torch/the parent arch, and no branch on command text. Nothing resolves a move chain in Python. The mechanism is genuinely learned: every address, gate and decay is a function of the frozen embeddings, and a wrong address returns wrong content that the same loss punishes. Causality at the scored position is clean and was verified by execution: corrupting obs_3 leaves the predictions at cmd_0..cmd_3 EXACTLY unchanged (delta 0.0 at all four) while changing cmd_4 (0.345); perturbing every padded slot after each row's read, including the withheld-observation slot immediately after it, changes the prediction at the read by exactly 0.0 for rows of depth 4, 3 and 2. The train/score asymmetry (command present, observation absent) is structurally unreachable at the read: g_write[i] is multiplied by live_obs[i] but only enters mem for steps > i, and `stored` is an exclusive cumsum, so the read position's own contribution never sees its own observation-presence flag.
summary: The code does implement the mechanism the hypothesis describes, and the central architectural claim is verifiable rather than aspirational. Driving net._transport_reads directly with ideal addresses and gates: a chain `cat A; mv A B; mv B C; mv C D; cat D` returns the content written at A with cosine 1.000000 and exact norm at the final read, taken before that step's own update. With realistic interference — dense random unit addresses in key_d=64, 10 files with distractor writes and distractor moves — the read still picks the correct content 20/20 at depths 1, 3 and 4, with retrieval cosine flat across depth (0.813/0.799/0.806 at 10 files). So "a single lookup at address(P), identical work at depth 1 and depth 8" is a real property of this code, and it is reachable at the scored command position with gradient from step 1. The three divergences are all overstatements in prose rather than mismatches in implementation: (1) the archived DESCRIPTION asserts as structural a role-address collapse on single-path commands that nothing in the code enforces; (2) the conditioning argument against multi-hop attention is stated unconditionally but is multiplicative in g_move exactly as attention is in softmax mass, and at the author's chosen init bias the depth-4 transport signal is 0.004 of the content with its gradient ~4700x weaker than at depth 1; (3) the compute estimate is off — measured 1.55x fwd+bwd on CPU, not "a small fraction". No numbers were falsely presented as measured: the author correctly hedges the memory/compute figure and explicitly says the decisive address-separation assumption is unmeasured. The one factual claim asserted about the corpus (mv observations are the same constant vector, so all routing lives in the command) is true. WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK: (a) the decisive assumption itself — whether the frozen mean-pooled embedding of `mv Q P` separates its first path from its second, and whether a_dst(`mv Q P`) ties to a_dst(`cat P`). The pinned eye (TJ_FT_ENCODER, HF veryfansome/terminal-jepa-encoders subfolder e5-nocwd) is not downloaded on this box, only the refs. A PROXY using the base encoder intfloat/e5-base-v2 and a head with this arch's exact shape (LN -> 768->176 -> GELU -> two 176->64 -> unit-normalize, matched against a codebook) on 90 synthetic `mv A B` over 10 real-looking paths: destination-path accuracy 0.32, source-path 0.43 against chance 0.10; a plain linear probe on the raw embedding gives dst 0.25 vs src 0.68; and a dst head trained on mv commands transfers to `cat P` at chance (0.10). Indicative that the role split is weak and the cross-role tie is not free — the author's own stated bottleneck looks real — but NOT decisive, because the actual eye is fine-tuned on this corpus and real training supervises both command types jointly through the task loss rather than through my classification probe. (b) I ran no training, so nothing about whether g_move actually rises, whether the depth-1 -> depth-4 transfer story holds, or what happens to comp_ca. Given the measured 0.0227 noise floor, a single three-seed draw will not settle that either. Work files are at /tmp/rev28/ (t1-t8.py, probe.py, probe2.py); nothing in the repo was modified.

divergences.claim: DESCRIPTION (the text archived with the genome): "The move update is identically zero whenever the two role addresses coincide, so single-path commands leave the store untouched."
divergences.what_the_code_does: Nothing in the code makes a single-path command produce coincident role addresses. a_src = unit(P_share f + P_src f) and a_dst = unit(P_share f + P_dst f) are computed from the SAME f for every command; they coincide only if the learned P_src and P_dst happen to agree on that f. At init the measured role cosine averages 0.50 (min 0.19, max 0.73), i.e. they do not coincide. Separately, the store is not "untouched" on a single-path command in any case: g_write still delta-rule-writes the observation at a_dst and lam still decays the whole store — which is the intended `cat X` behaviour described elsewhere in the same hypothesis. The hypothesis BODY is honest about this (it lists address collapse as a failure mode); only the archived DESCRIPTION states it as a structural property.
divergences.evidence: Read of evolve/chunks/arch/r25_address_transport_memory.py:_role_addresses + forward; measured at init on random input: role cos mean 0.4981 / min 0.1924 / max 0.7288 (/tmp/rev28/t7.py).

divergences.claim: "(2) Conditioning. ... a chain of rank-one updates that is LINEAR in the stored observation vector, with unit-norm addresses and a decay near 1, so gradient reaches an early write with roughly constant magnitude regardless of how many moves intervene. A multi-hop attention chase multiplies several softmax distributions, and both the forward error and the gradient degrade with each hop."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The transported content is multiplied by g_move at EVERY hop (moved = g_move * (v_src - v_dst)), so the channel is exactly as multiplicative in the move gate as an attention chase is in softmax mass. The claimed conditioning advantage holds only in the saturated limit g_move -> 1, which the model must learn. Executed on the real _transport_reads: with g_move=g_erase=1 and lam=0.995, cos(read, content)=1.0000 at every depth and the norm ratio is 0.89/1.04/0.98/0.91/0.67/0.63 at depths 1/2/3/4/6/8, with the gradient to the early write roughly flat through depth 4 — the claim holds there. At the author's own init bias g_move=0.269, the same measurement gives norm ratio 0.295/0.092/0.054/0.004 at depths 1/2/3/4 and the gradient to the early write drops from 2.35 to 0.0005 (~4700x) between depth 1 and depth 4 — i.e. on the eligible slice (depths 3-4) the transport channel starts essentially silent and gets almost no direct gradient, and must be bootstrapped by depth-1 windows exactly as the hypothesis hopes. The gate-stall risk is listed by the author, but the conditioning argument is stated unqualified.
divergences.evidence: /tmp/rev28/t5.py, driving net._transport_reads in float64 with hand-set gates and unit addresses.

divergences.claim: "Cost: the module adds a second sequential loop over the ~31 command steps ... I estimate this at a few hundred megabytes of extra activation at batch 64 and a small fraction of a step's compute, but I could not run it here, so this is an estimate and not a measurement."
divergences.what_the_code_does: Measured fwd+bwd wall clock at B=16, L=61 on CPU: parent r22 0.199 s, this candidate 0.308 s — 1.55x, not a small fraction. The activation estimate is about right for the store alone (31 steps x 64x64x768 fp32 ~ 390 MB at batch 64) but does not count the per-step bmm intermediates. Properly hedged as an estimate by the author, so this is a calibration note rather than a false claim; it matters for the round budget, not for validity.
divergences.evidence: /tmp/rev28/t7.py; sequence lengths in data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat/train.jsonl are 26-32 steps, so the "~31" figure is accurate.
